body: I can reproduce this on 4.4.1 and it still happens with #105746 applied. Have not tested yet if #106490 makes a difference but I expect it won't.

> Have not tested yet if [#106490](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/106490) makes a difference but I expect it won't.

It does not.

There's something odd going on in this MRP though. I made an attempt at simplifying it down to just the actual bodies and shapes, without the `@tool` scripts and Blender import, and now the problem went away for the ladder/fence thing, but the egg issue does however remain when using Jolt: [jolt-egg-mrp-2.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20391024/jolt-egg-mrp-2.zip)

EDIT: I simplified it some more, and updated my MRP link, but egg issue remains.

@jrouwe I went back a couple of Jolt versions with the extension, while changing nothing else of relevance, and assuming I didn't make some mistake in this process, it seems this regression came about somewhere in this range of commits: _[REDACTED]_

EDIT: Nevermind, I did mess up after all. The range of commits was wrong. Let me just pinpoint the exact commit instead.

I got the range wrong after all, so I bisected the actual commit instead, and it seems the regression stems from: jrouwe/JoltPhysics#1500

Sure enough, disabling the `physics/jolt_physics_3d/simulation/use_enhanced_internal_edge_removal` project setting (which just disables `JPH::BodyCreationSettings::mEnhancedInternalEdgeRemoval` for the static bodies) resolves the issue.

Should internal edge removal even be used in this context, given that the sensors have it disabled? I would have thought that both bodies would need to have it enabled for it to be used.

Currently the implementation is that if either one of the bodies/sensors has enhanced internal edge removal turned on, then it will be on for the pair. You may be right that edge removal should be turned off for sensors, but it is kind of an odd rule. Especially the fact that from a `ContactListener` you can turn a regular body into a sensor (by which time the decision to do enhanced internal edge removal is long done) makes it a bit weird.

Without looking at this in detail, I suspect that the problem here is that the 'egg' is deeply embedded in the sensor so that the face is finds is kind of random (it should be the deepest, but that is not very well defined for concave shapes). Without internal edge removal it will report overlap for all sub shapes and with internal edge removal many of those sub shapes will get removed as they are internal edges. This means you get an exit for one sub shape and an enter for another as the sensor moves, which I believe is what we're seeing here (adding a `print` to `_process` seems to confirm this). Before https://github.com/jrouwe/JoltPhysics/pull/1500 internal edge removal didn't work properly on these dense meshes so you would get most of the hits reported anyway.

I suspect the fix for this problem is to fix up #105746 so that it deals with changing sub shape IDs (see: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/105746#issuecomment-2831187068 and your remarks following it).

I can look into this a bit deeper tomorrow if you want.

> I suspect the fix for this problem is to fix up [#105746](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/105746) so that it deals with changing sub shape IDs (see: [#105746 (comment)](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/105746#issuecomment-2831187068) and your remarks following it).

Makes sense.

> I can look into this a bit deeper tomorrow if you want.

It'd be great to have confirmed that this is indeed the problem. Then I can look into fixing the changing sub-shape ID thing for #105746.

To further simplify, I only exported the 'egg' to the Jolt samples and added some code to draw the contacts:

[LoadSnapshotTest.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20417000/LoadSnapshotTest.zip)

With the old `InternalEdgeRemovingCollector` this looks like this:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2d7c5f6c-7aee-4f44-9e70-02f9117bb199

With the new one it looks like:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e29734a0-8ae9-4b37-8a1e-527c76887c2a

So:

* With the old collector it was clearly overflowing the internal buffer causing many internal edges to be returned meaning the SubShapeIDs were reasonably constant.
* With the new collector it works much better, but you can see that it jitters between 2 faces when the cylinder is moving because these faces are symmetrical so they are both equally deep/valid.
* It also shows that in both cases the egg is not detected by the cylinder when the cylinder is roughly in the center, this is because every face of the egg is backfacing at this time so they're all discarded.

I think this shows what I suspected earlier:

* We should fix #105746 so that it can deal with changing sub shape IDs between a body pair.
* Additionally, in the `SimCollideBodyVsBody` override when handling a sensor we should also set `p_collide_shape_settings.mBackFaceMode = EBackFaceMode::CollideWithBackFaces` so that we report all hits.

> I think this shows what I suspected earlier

Great, thank you for confirming!

> Additionally, in the `SimCollideBodyVsBody` override when handling a sensor we should also set `p_collide_shape_settings.mBackFaceMode = EBackFaceMode::CollideWithBackFaces` so that we report all hits.

We already wrap every sensor with our custom "double-sided" decorator shape:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/45fc515ae3574e9c1f9deacaa6960dec68a7d38b/modules/jolt_physics/objects/jolt_shaped_object_3d.cpp#L76-L78

So it presumably only behaves this way in `LoadSnapshotTest` because those decorator shapes are discarded from the snapshot.

> So it presumably only behaves this way in `LoadSnapshotTest` because those decorator shapes are discarded from the snapshot.

So apparently this ends up not actually being the case when using `JPH::CollideShapeVsShapePerLeaf`, because the shape gets stripped down to its leaf shapes, which includes stripping away any decorator shapes.

Obviously this isn't so much a problem for decorator shapes that get "baked into" the result of `JPH::TransformedShape::CollectTransformedShapes`, like `JPH::RotatedTranslatedShape` and whatnot, but for decorator shapes that are purely meant to affect the collision detection it's more of a problem.

---

Anyway, if we ignore that part for now, it turns out that fixing this MRP in terms of the body enter/exit signals is as simple as doing what I had talked about [here](https://github.com/jrouwe/JoltPhysics/discussions/1476#discussioncomment-11955014), which is to simply swap the order of these two event reporting loops:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/45fc515ae3574e9c1f9deacaa6960dec68a7d38b/modules/jolt_physics/objects/jolt_area_3d.cpp#L146-L152

That way the `AREA_BODY_ADDED` events gets flushed first, which increments the reference counter on the scene side of things, as seen here:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/45fc515ae3574e9c1f9deacaa6960dec68a7d38b/scene/3d/physics/area_3d.cpp#L266

... which prevents the reference counter from hitting zero once the remove event gets flushed, which would otherwise have emitted the `body_exited` signal, as seen here:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/45fc515ae3574e9c1f9deacaa6960dec68a7d38b/scene/3d/physics/area_3d.cpp#L283-L292

However... It seems that this is quite a bit messier than that, and I fear that this has probably always been broken, but has somehow miraculously gone unnoticed until now.

If you connect callbacks to the Area3D's `body_shape_entered` and `body_shape_exited` signals you'll see that you still get showered in enter and exit events as you pass through the egg, where `body_shape_index` is `0` and `local_shape_index` is `0` for all of them, regardless if you have enhanced internal edge removal enabled or not.

The reason for this seems to be that I somehow assumed that one `JPH::SubShapeID` equals one `JPH::Shape`, which is obviously not the case with individual triangles of `JPH::MeshShape`. These pairs of `JPH::SubShapeID` then all have events queued up for them, but since they all resolve to a `JoltArea3D::ShapeIndexPair` of `(0, 0)` (because of [this](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/45fc515ae3574e9c1f9deacaa6960dec68a7d38b/modules/jolt_physics/shapes/jolt_custom_user_data_shape.h#L57)) you just get a ton of those events being sent off all the time, which is just wrong.

I am frankly in mild disbelief over this, but I guess sensors weren't even able to interact with `JPH::MeshShape` when I first implemented support for `Area3D`, so I suppose I have some excuse at least.

So I will most likely have to refactor `JoltArea3D` in some way, like immediately resolve every `JPH::SubShapeID` pair down to a `JoltArea3D::ShapeIndexPair` and do some kind of reference counting, and only emit the relevant events based on the value of that reference counter, similar to how it's done in the `Area3D` scene node.

The only problem with that is that I can't reasonably get the shape indices for a body that's been removed from the `JPH::PhysicsSystem`, so I'll probably have to base it around `JPH::SubShapeID` pairs in some way anyway.

What a mess. 😅

> So apparently this ends up not actually being the case when using `JPH::CollideShapeVsShapePerLeaf`, because the shape gets stripped down to its leaf shapes, which includes stripping away any decorator shapes.

I'm realizing now that this is largely my own fault, and within my power to change the behavior of, by simply overriding these methods in a better way:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/45fc515ae3574e9c1f9deacaa6960dec68a7d38b/modules/jolt_physics/shapes/jolt_custom_decorated_shape.h#L81-L83

I'm assuming I can just make a "decorating collector" that wraps the actual collector and puts the decorator shape back onto the resulting `JPH::TransformedShape::mShape` within its own `AddHit` implementation?

> The only problem with that is that I can't reasonably get the shape indices for a body that's been removed from the JPH::PhysicsSystem, so I'll probably have to base it around JPH::SubShapeID pairs in some way anyway.

I think it is indeed safer to do ref counting based on `SubShapeID` pairs (and remember the shape index when the contact is added), but an added complexity there is that these may also change if the shape of a body changes (e.g. when a `CollisionShape3D` is added/removed). Luckily you have `JoltBody3D::areas` so in theory you could update the bookkeeping of an area if a body is changed, but it sounds quite complex to do this reliably.

> I'm assuming I can just make a "decorating collector" that wraps the actual collector and puts the decorator shape back onto the resulting JPH::TransformedShape::mShape within its own AddHit implementation?

I think that would be possible, but not very efficient as you would be allocating lots of shapes in a collector. If the `JoltCustomDoubleSidedShape`s are always inserted just before the leaf shapes (i.e. you don't have a `CompoundShape` decorated with a `JoltCustomDoubleSidedShape` but there is one `JoltCustomDoubleSidedShape` per child of the compound instead) then you can implement those two functions as `Shape` does, basically returning a `JoltCustomDoubleSidedShape` with a shape instead of a leaf shape.

A simpler way may be what I initially suggested of setting `p_collide_shape_settings.mBackFaceMode = EBackFaceMode::CollideWithBackFaces` before calling `CollideShapeVsShapePerLeaf`. I don't think we care about double sided for the purpose of area overlaps, any overlap should be reported. So we don't need `JoltCustomDoubleSidedShape`s to selectively turn double sided on/off.

> but an added complexity there is that these may also change if the shape of a body changes (e.g. when a `CollisionShape3D` is added/removed). Luckily you have `JoltBody3D::areas` so in theory you could update the bookkeeping of an area if a body is changed, but it sounds quite complex to do this reliably.

Yeah, stuff like this keeps me up at night. It's basically asking for stale data.

I'll need to find time to explore all this properly, ideally before the looming 4.5-rc1, but that might be a tall order.

> If the `JoltCustomDoubleSidedShape`s are always inserted just before the leaf shapes (i.e. you don't have a `CompoundShape` decorated with a `JoltCustomDoubleSidedShape` but there is one `JoltCustomDoubleSidedShape` per child of the compound instead)

That is unfortunately not the case. An `Area3D` applies the `JoltCustomDoubleSidedShape` as the outermost shape, meaning it decorates the compound shape in the case where it has more than one shape.

> A simpler way may be what I initially suggested of setting `p_collide_shape_settings.mBackFaceMode = EBackFaceMode::CollideWithBackFaces` before calling `CollideShapeVsShapePerLeaf`. I don't think we care about double sided for the purpose of area overlaps, any overlap should be reported. So we don't need `JoltCustomDoubleSidedShape`s to selectively turn double sided on/off.

Yeah, that might be the simpler fix to this specific problem. Unfortunately we still need the decorator shape as well, since `Area3D` can have physics queries performed against it in much the same way as you can with regular physics bodies.

> I'll need to find time to explore all this properly, ideally before the looming 4.5-rc1, but that might be a tall order.

I would say it's broken now too. I think there is an easy way to at least unbreak it for the case where people are not adding/removing shapes by tracking sub shape IDs and not bothering about updating the data structure on shape changes. The worst thing that can happen is that you send the wrong shape index in the `AREA_BODY_REMOVED` callback but that value isn't even passed on to the body_entered/exited callbacks. And when replacing a shape with another shape, you won't get a removed then readded callback as most likely the sub shape IDs remain the same. There's no risk of actually missing contact removals as Jolt will send contact remove callbacks for sub shape IDs that were removed.

> Unfortunately we still need the decorator shape as well, since Area3D can have physics queries performed against it in much the same way as you can with regular physics bodies.

Yes, and I think it's perfectly fine to keep them. The `CollectTransformedShapes` and `TransformShape` are barely used by Jolt. I did a quick scan and I think the first is only used by soft bodies, but soft bodies will never support double sided meshes as you can't test a point against a triangle and hope that it exactly overlaps with the triangle as we're discretely time stepping the simulation. The 2nd function I believe is only used to scale shapes, in which case you could rewrap the shape with a double sided shape if needed.

> I would say it's broken now too.

For sure. I didn't mean to imply that it would make things any worse necessarily, just that me getting that stuff right (with the limited time I have available these days) might be tough.

> The worst thing that can happen is that you send the wrong shape index in the `AREA_BODY_REMOVED` callback but that value isn't even passed on to the body_entered/exited callbacks.

They are passed to the `body_shape_entered` and `body_shape_exited` (and `area_shape_*` equivalent) signals though. The shape index pairs are also cached in `Area3D::BodyState::shapes`, so ideally should be reported correctly so as to clean that up, but I don't know if that's worth getting hung up on.

> The 2nd function I believe is only used to scale shapes, in which case you could rewrap the shape with a double sided shape if needed.

Right, yeah, that one should be an easy fix.

---

The more I think about all this, I'm realizing that I think we actually have all the pieces in place already to make this not that big of a deal after all. In fact, I took a stab at a naive implementation of adding this reference counting, and at least as far as the MRPs here are concerned [this](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/compare/master...mihe:godot:a8ae0a610ccf25ef2f494de26b98b8954395d458) seems to fix all of the problems, with [this](https://github.com/mihe/godot/commit/a8ae0a610ccf25ef2f494de26b98b8954395d458) commit being the interesting one.

(Note that I've based that branch on top of #105746 and #106693. The latter was just to make things easier to reason about.)

There's probably some more efficient way of doing the same thing, but it's not terrible as-is I guess. It basically just boils down to assuming that there will be duplicate shape index pairs in the existing `JoltArea3D::Overlap::shape_pairs` and to only have the pending shape index pairs in `JoltArea3D::Overlap::pending_added` and `JoltArea3D::Overlap::pending_removed` turn into actual "downstream" events if they change the reference counter (at the time of flushing the events) to or from zero, and once again making sure to flush `AREA_BODY_ADDED` before `AREA_BODY_REMOVED`.

I haven't tested changing the shapes of the area itself and/or the shapes of the object it overlaps, but I _think_ that will actually get taken care of properly by `JoltContactListener3D::_flush_area_shifts`. I need to do more testing to make sure though.

Feel free to test it out yourself.

Since this uses shape index pairs as key for `refs_by_indices` and since `_add_shape_pair` will update the SubShapeID to shape index map for every contact that gets reported, I think that when the shape changes that it is possible that the ref count of a different `refs_by_indices` entry can get decremented on contact remove than the one that was incremented during contact add.

I would say that you either need to:
* Use SubShapeIDs as key in `ref_by_indices` and have the shape index pairs + ref count as value.
* Only set the shape index pairs in `_add_shape_pair` on `shape_pairs` when the first contact for that pair is reported and keep the values constant until the pair is removed again from the map.

> I think that when the shape changes that it is possible that the ref count of a different `refs_by_indices` entry can get decremented on contact remove than the one that was incremented during contact add. This is/was in my mind the scenario that `JoltContactListener3D::_flush_area_shifts` was meant to mitigate, as any `JPH::SubShapeID` that no longer points to the same (globally incremented/unique) `JoltShapeInstance3D::id` (i.e. the user data) as what was seen in the previous frame would be forced to go through the process of exiting and re-entering the `JoltArea3D`. The `JoltContactListener3D::area_exits`, which are all processed before `JoltContactListener3D::area_enters` in `JoltContactListener3D::post_step`, would in that case use the shape index pair previously cached in the overlap, so would be correct, and the `area_enters` would, as you mentioned, always update the shape indices as part of `JoltArea3D::_add_shape_pair`, so would then also be correct[^1]. However, it seems that `_flush_area_shifts` was also broken, in multiple places even. To start with, the fact that I had put this in `JoltContactListener3D::post_step` was not correct at all, as it then also ran on shape addition/removals, which would understandably cause `JPH::CompoundShape::GetSubShapeUserData` to throw asserts about invalid IDs for one of the two compound shapes. I should have at the very least checked that the `JPH::SubShapeID` was valid for both of them (and that they were in fact both compound shapes to begin with). How this has gone unnoticed for over two years now, by myself most of all, I'll never know. A much better place for it, which I'm fairly sure I tried before I pushed all this stuff to GitHub way back when, is [what you suggested](https://github.com/jrouwe/JoltPhysics/discussions/433#discussioncomment-4934894) and stick this stuff in `OnContactPersisted` instead. There's a good spot for it in the `evaluate` lambda in `JoltContactListener3D::_try_evaluate_area_overlap`, which also means we're no longer looping over every single area contact every single physics step. On top of that I had apparently introduced a regression to `_flush_area_shifts`, as part of #101189, which is that this mutable-to-static compound shape "upgrade" should not in fact overwrite `JoltShapedObject3D::previous_jolt_shape` as part of rebuilding the shape tree the second time around. In fact, only the first shape change per step should write to `previous_jolt_shape`, otherwise we obviously end up comparing against the wrong previous shape in the contact listener, which caused all kinds of weird errors. With those fixes, plus the reference counting largely unchanged from my previous comment, I am seemingly able to add/remove/move shapes around in its parent's array of shapes, whilst overlapping with an Area3D, and the final Area3D signal emissions at least make some kind of sense now. You'll find the complete changes here: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/compare/master...mihe:godot:jolt/area-ref-count (without #105746 this time around) --- There is however one problem with this latest version, depending on how you look at it, which you'll find in this fairly simple example project, where it just removes a bunch of shapes from "the middle" of the shape array: [area-shape-shifts.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20492540/area-shape-shifts.zip) The output from this when running with Godot Physics is as follows:

'MyRigidBody' shape at index 1 exited ```

... which makes some kind of sense to me. If you're removing from the middle of the array, shifting subsequent elements leftward, it's arguably somewhat correct to first remove that index, along with all the subsequent ones, before adding them back at their shifted indices. That way you can connect to these signals and actually mirror these operations somewhere else and end up with the same final state. However, when you run this with Jolt with my most recent change, you get this instead:
[Click to expand]

``` [MyArea] 'MyRigidBody' entered [MyArea] 'MyRigidBody' shape at index 6 entered [MyArea] 'MyRigidBody' shape at index 5 entered [MyArea] 'MyRigidBody' shape at index 4 entered [MyArea] 'MyRigidBody' shape at index 3 entered [MyArea] 'MyRigidBody' shape at index 2 entered [MyArea] 'MyRigidBody' shape at index 1 entered [MyArea] 'MyRigidBody' shape at index 0 entered [MyRigidBody] ---- Removing shape at index 1 ---- [MyArea] 'MyRigidBody' shape at index 6 exited [MyRigidBody] ---- Removing shape at index 1 ---- [MyArea] 'MyRigidBody' shape at index 5 exited [MyRigidBody] ---- Removing shape at index 1 ---- [MyArea] 'MyRigidBody' shape at index 4 exited [MyRigidBody] ---- Removing shape at index 1 ---- [MyArea] 'MyRigidBody' shape at index 3 exited [MyRigidBody] ---- Removing shape at index 1 ---- [MyArea] 'MyRigidBody' shape at index 2 exited [MyRigidBody] ---- Removing shape at index 1 ---- [MyArea] 'MyRigidBody' shape at index 1 exited ```

... which while maybe not strictly incorrect, is probably not ideal, since you don't in fact get notified of all the changes that are happening, which means you can't use these signal emissions to mirror the state changes somewhere else. It's not clear to me how to fix that exactly, and I don't think it's worth holding this up from becoming a pull request, but I figured I should mention it. [^1]: I'm not sure if this constant updating of the shape indices is strictly necessary though. I think I threw that in mostly to lessen the likelihood of stale indices, but I suppose that is pretty wasteful in hindsight, and arguably isn't any more "correct" anyway.

I went ahead and turned this latest iteration into a PR: #106918

I figured it's at least better than the current behavior, and would seem to resolve the issue here, but if you see any room for improvement I'm curious to hear it of course.
